newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to raise foreign funds in two only mkts.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to raise foreign funds in two only mkts.

text.p: South Africa would raise four billion rand of foreign loans in 1997/98 (April-March) in only two markets, finance department director general Maria Ramos said on Wednesday.
She did not say which foreign markets would be selected.
Briefing the parliamentary finance committee, Ramos said South Africa remained cautious about foreign borrowings.
"We...are quite cautious of taking on board excessive foreign exchange risk," she said.
"So we have begun our forays into the foreign capital markets quite cautiously. We have tried to keep foreign borrowing at around four to five percent of our total portfolio."
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced in his budget last week that the government intended to raise 4.0 billion of foreign loans in the next fiscal year, up from 2.8 billion in 1996/97.
The government expects to raise 27.7 billion rand from the domestic market in 1997/98, against 34.2 billion in 1996/97.
South Africa has borrowed abroad since the 1994 elections with the aim of opening up markets closed to it under sanctions and to establish benchmarks.
It has also tried to borrow in the currencies which dominate the basket of currencies used to determine the effective real exchange rate of the rand.
But the domestic market had been liquid enough to support most of government's borrowing requirements, Ramos said.
"We constantly look at that and, as we go forward, these ratios may change a little bit but I think that...we simply could not go out on a foreign borrowing spree."
